newsitem.title: USA: Endocardial files for heart test system.
newsitem.headline: Endocardial files for heart test system.

text.p: Endocardial Solutions Inc said it submitted an application for an investigational device exemption, or IDE, to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration for its heart diagnostic system.
The application covers use of the company's EnSite 3000 and EnSite catheter in the right atrium of the heart in a multi-center clinical study, it said.

"During the IPO we told investors we expected to receive authorization from the FDA to expand our clinical trials in the left ventricle and we planned to submit an IDE for use of our EnSite product in the right atrium during the second quarter," said chief executive Jim Bullock.
"I am very pleased to say that we have accomplished both of these significant milestones and are looking forward to continued clinical validation of our system," Bullock said.

Endocardial's cardiac diagnostic system, which provides a 3-D graphical display of the heart's electrical activity, is designed to help physicians diagnose potentially life-threatening arrhythmias, or abnormally rapid heartbeats caused by irregular electrical activity in the heart.
